Guards this morning: 'Family Fare 3972 rows | 32% re-verified against the store TODAY (1259 of 3972 dated) | file 0d old'.

The alert still fires because pull-regular-familyfare's throttle-wipeout ALERT compares one run's raw collection (701 items at 01:05) against best-of-recent (3787). Under 3-hourly sharded sweeps a single run collects a SLICE by design, so this comparison can NEVER pass again - a permanent daily false page on an architecture that is working.

Real residual defect: every sweep ends 'ABORTING - 60 consecutive empty terms ... HTTP 400 x~180' and then advances the cursor PAST the whole attempted range ('this run bought terms #154..#243' -> cursor #244), so the ~60 terms inside the 400 wall are skipped, not retried next window. The 'still empty' ledger plateaus at ~466 terms (432 -> 454 -> 464 -> 466 -> 468 -> 466 -> 466) and includes staples FF certainly carries: oat milk, hot dog buns, feta cheese crumbled, microwave popcorn, tomato soup.

surface_fix.what: stop the false daily page: re-key the throttle ALERT on outcomes, not per-run collection

root_fix.what: cursor honesty: on abort, advance the cursor only to the START of the consecutive-failure wall (first term of the empty/400 streak), so next window's fresh budget resumes exactly where the store cut us off; walled terms get first claim instead of being skipped for a full wrap

items.deviation: SURFACE FIX SHIPPED AS PLANNED; ROOT FIX DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED - ITS PREMISE IS FALSE. The plan states that on ABORT the cursor 'advances PAST the whole attempted range (this run bought terms #154..#243 -> cursor #244), so the ~60 terms inside the 400 wall are skipped'. Read against the code and the log, that is a misreading of the log line. \ is the last term that RETURNED PRODUCTS, and any success resets \ - so on abort next_index = last-success+1 IS the first term of the 60-term wall, which is exactly the behaviour the root_fix asks for. Confirmed end-to-end in ff-sweep-log.txt: the 04:00 run bought #154..#243 and wrote #244; the 07:00 run then STARTED at #244 and came back with 773 fresh rows - the walled tail was retried, not skipped. Changing it would have moved the cursor backwards into terms already bought. The ~466 'still empty' plateau is therefore NOT starvation: line 216 adds every UNATTEMPTED remaining term to the empty ledger, so under a sharded sweep that buys ~88 of 526 terms the ledger is ~438 unreached + ~28 genuinely empty by construction. It is a reporting artifact of the sweep architecture, and it will NOT trend down - the plan's 24h bounce-back trigger would have fired on correct behaviour. INSTEAD OF THE NO-OP CHANGE: the cursor arithmetic was lifted into Get-FfNextCursor and pinned with 5 frozen self-test cases (including the plan's exact must-fire, #154+89 -> #244, which passes on today's code), so the invariant the plan doubted is now provable instead of arguable.
